audit.whatIsWrong: content win[5] and win[6] say 'Darius' and full phases[5]/[6].side say 'Darius', while the why text on those same rows says Dr. Mundo out-scales him; phases[4] is 'Skill' though the mirror audit already assigned Level 6 to Dr. Mundo.
audit.why: Dr. Mundo wins 55.84% over 3852 games, the packet chart gives him Level 6 onward, and the mirror audit (darius__drmundo) states Level 6, first item and two-plus items all belong to Dr. Mundo. The current sides contradict the win rate, the mirror and their own whys.
audit.corrected: Level 6, First item and 2+ items flipped to Dr. Mundo in both layers with ratings raised to match; Levels 1-2 stay Darius, Level 3 Skill, Levels 4-5 Darius.

audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is listed at 24s in two places; the real cooldown is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16. No sequencing numbers appear anywhere (the packet flags exactly this defect).
audit.why: The whole page tells you to commit on Apprehend's cooldown, so the number has to be right — 26s at rank 1 is a far bigger window than 24s, and 16s at rank 5 is a much smaller one.
audit.corrected: Apprehend written as 26s at rank 1 / 16s at rank 5, Decimate as 9s at rank 1, Maximum Dosage as 120s.
sources: champ-data/_kits darius E cd 26/23.5/21/18.5/16, Q cd 9/8/7/6/5

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text credits Maximum Dosage with a 'cleanse-like health swing'. It cleanses nothing — Riot's text is an instant heal of a percent of missing health plus move speed and regen. Nothing states that Noxian Guillotine's true damage makes armour the wrong answer, or that Decimate's heal needs Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage scaled to Hemorrhage stacks, so resistances do not reduce it; Decimate heals off blade hits on champions, which is what wins him extended trades. Both are in the _missing list for this matchup.
audit.corrected: R described as an instant missing-health heal best pressed after the execute lands; true-damage execute called out as resistance-proof; Bramble Vest / Grievous Wounds named against Decimate's heal.

edits.before: At 3 his full kit and Noxian Might potential dominate the trade.
edits.after: At 3 your passive eats his Apprehend pull once — even trade.

edits.before: This is Darius's window. His Q Decimate outer-blade heals him and his passive Hemorrhage bleed stacks fast; each stack ramps his damage and lets his W Crippling Strike hit harder. Don't stand in the outer ring of his Q and don't let five bleed stacks land, or his Noxian Might turns every auto into a huge hit.
edits.after: This is Darius's window. Decimate (Q) heals off the outer blade every 9s at rank 1 and Hemorrhage stacks to five, where Noxian Might turns every auto into a huge hit. Stay out of the blade ring, and buy an early Grievous Wounds source — Bramble Vest is what stops his Q healing straight back through your trade.

edits.before: Darius R Noxian Guillotine executes off bleed stacks, but your R Maximum Dosage heal and the cleanse-like health swing lets you survive the first cast. Ult reactively when he goes for the execute and you often live, flipping the fight.
edits.after: Noxian Guillotine (R) is true damage scaled to bleed stacks, so armour does nothing for it. Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percent of your missing health — press it after the execute lands, not before, and you live through the cast and deny him the reset.

edits.before: - Darius Apprehend (Pull) (24s): matchup-defining — His all-in starts on the pull. Don’t get caught. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Darius Apprehend (Pull) (26s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5): matchup-defining — his all-in starts on the pull, and your passive absorbs it once. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate (120s): spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call.

edits.before: Track Darius’s Apprehend (Pull) (24s): His all-in starts on the pull. Don’t get caught. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Darius’s Apprehend (Pull) (26s at rank 1): your passive absorbs the pull once, then it’s down or you don’t go.

notes: diffRating and carryRating were empty strings while breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both state 6/10 and 6/10 — filled to match the prose. Open question carried over from the mirror audit and NOT resolved here: several fields imply Mundo's passive 'cleanses' or 'blocks' Apprehend. Riot's text says he resists the first Immobilizing effect, so I wrote 'absorbs it once' — whether Apprehend's pull counts as immobilizing for that purpose is not settled by the kit data.
